answer: No. Because your brother is on active military deployment, he can sign the deployed owner authorization, form NW-MIL-1, instead of a notarized power of attorney. NW-MIL-1 is accepted in Georgia even though other powers of attorney there, including NW-POA-2, must be notarized. He signs it electronically and attaches a copy of his deployment orders, and you'll still need to bring your own photo ID to the appointment.
